findings.where: Screens 7-10 (delta, power), circuit drawing, title row and explain paragraph 1
findings.what: Only the loads switch to delta, while the supply stays three coils joined at a drawn star point under the unchanged subtitle '230 V a winding'. Screen 7 says 'with no star point and no neutral', and V_ph silently becomes the load's 398.4 V. Explain paragraph 1 says joining the windings nose to tail puts the √3 on the current, which the picture never shows. So the line-or-phase distinction the lesson exists to teach becomes ambiguous. Label the left side 'supply, in star, 230 V a winding' and add one line saying the supply stays in star and 'phase' now means one load.

findings.where: Screen 12 (Mixed: a delta motor), circuit drawing
findings.what: The only coil symbols drawn are the supply's windings, which are in star and so carry the clamp's 26 A, while the motor's windings are drawn as plain load boxes. From the picture, '26 A' is a defensible answer to 'what current flows in each winding?', and its hint 'That is star's rule' does not settle it. Draw the motor's windings as coils, or label the left side 'supply'.

findings.where: Screen 11 (Mixed: a board), the two 3 × V_ph × I_ph × cos φ readouts after a right Check; also screen 9's delta readout
findings.what: Worked by hand from the factors shown, 'star: 3 × 230.9 × 20 × 0.85 = 11,778 W' gives 11,776 W and 'delta: 3 × 400 × 11.55 × 0.85 = 11,778 W' gives 11,781 W, and screen 9's '3 × 398.4 × 17.32 × 0.8 = 16,560 W' gives 16,561 W. The results come from unrounded values, so the shown sums do not equal the shown answers. Either compute from the displayed factors or add 'the same but for rounding', as the practice worked example already does.

findings.where: Screens 2, 6, 8 and 10 (the DO screens after each SHOW)
findings.what: Each puzzle asks for a number the screen just before stated outright: 398.4 V, 'the neutral carries 10 A minus L3's current', 30.0 A, and 5520 W to 16,560 W. They test recall of the last screen, not use of the rule. Change the case, for example ask for the L2-L3 reading, L3 at 7 A, or a different load, so Dan has to apply the idea.

findings.where: Key under the arrows on screens 1, 2, 8 and 12
findings.what: The key entry 'an arrow turned half round' shows a dashed swatch before any dashed arrow is on screen. On the puzzle screens it stays there until a right Check, so the key names something that is not there; show the entry only once the dashed copy appears.

Neither star point is labelled, although the text keeps referring to 'the star point'. The neutral also leaves the loads' star point along the same horizontal as L2's load, so L2, its load and the neutral read as one straight wire. Label 'star point' at both ends and drop the neutral's start below L2's line.
'For the course's puzzle, each phase has its own power triangle' refers to lesson 8's motor question without saying so and reads as a stray phrase here; write 'As in lesson 8's motor puzzle, ...'.

'Which the trade rounds to the 400 V nominal of a UK three-phase board': the 400 V is listed as a constant with no source, and ENA's quote covers only 230 V. Cite a 230/400 V source, or say it is the 400 V he reads at the board.

'Prove dead between every pair of lines as well as each line to neutral and earth' is unsourced and re-teaches safe isolation, which his inspection and testing qualifications cover. Keep only the reminder that about 400 V sits between lines.

findings.where: Screen 4 Why, explain paragraph 2 and closing line
findings.what: The brief promised a sourced line that many ships run three wires with no neutral (notes 6.1, SECONDARY), with the NAVSEA 450 V delta load as an example. It also promised Kuphaldt's trade-off: star gives 'the same amount of power with less line current' and delta 'greater reliability in the event of winding failure'. Neither appears. One line after 'fed by the three lines alone' would tie the idea to his Navy path.

Both mixed puzzles are three-phase only. The brief asked the last screens to mix the whole course so Dan chooses the tool first, for example the peak of a 400 V line voltage, or kVA from line readings and a power factor.
The clamp reads 'I_L = 10.00 A', '30.00 A' and '26.00 A' while the text, rows and answer buttons say 10 A, 30.0 A and 26 A; match the precision.

The opening paragraph runs to about 14 lines at 360 px and pushes the picture below the fold. The demo waits until the picture is in view, but the brief asks for words to stay short where the picture carries them. Move the 'pass back down L2's winding' sentence to screen 2's Why.
